sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Two-way if-else statements help your program make decisions between two options. It's like choosing between two doors - only one path gets taken!

• How to write if-else statements
• When to use two-way decisions
• How to handle yes/no situations in code

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're at a traffic light. If it's green, you go. If it's red, you stop. That's exactly how if-else works!

Two-way if-else statements let your program choose between two actions based on a condition:

• If the condition is true → do the first action
• If the condition is false → do the second action

Key Points
points: if-else provides two alternative paths: one when the condition is true, one when false
Exactly one of the two blocks will execute for any given input
Use if-else when you need to choose between two mutually exclusive actions
Always include braces {} for both the if and else blocks
The else clause must immediately follow the closing brace of the if body

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Two-way if-else makes decisions between two options. Always has one condition and two possible outcomes. Practice with simple yes/no scenarios first. Ready to learn about nested if-else next.
